summary: 48-year-old woman, 30 h of constant RUQ pain after a fatty meal, fever 38.2 °C, Murphy's sign, WBC 13.1, CRP 86, ultrasound shows gallstones with wall thickening and pericholecystic fluid. No Grade II/III criteria.

inputs.hpi: 30 hours of constant right upper quadrant pain that began after a fatty meal, radiating to the right shoulder tip. Nausea and vomiting twice. Previous brief similar episodes over 6 months; gallstones on a scan last year. Feels feverish. No jaundice, no dark urine, no pale stools. No rigors.

exam.general: Alert. Temperature 38.2°C, pulse 98/min, BP 134/84. Not jaundiced.
exam.abdomen: Tender in the right upper quadrant with a positive Murphy's sign and localised guarding; no palpable mass. No generalised peritonism. Bowel sounds present.

imaging.name: USS abdomen
imaging.result: Distended gallbladder with multiple gallstones and a stone impacted in the neck. Wall thickened to 5 mm with a thin rim of pericholecystic fluid. Sonographic Murphy's sign positive. CBD 5 mm, not dilated.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute calculous cholecystitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute calculous cholecystitis, Tokyo (TG18) Grade I (mild). No organ dysfunction, WCC below 18, symptoms under 72 h, no palpable mass.

mustRankTopK.note: TG18 definite diagnosis (local + systemic + imaging signs).
mustRankTopK.knownGapNote: iOS: fallback mode (DiagnosticDatabase.json does not decode): the gallstone ultrasound text is appended to the CC for routing and selects the biliaryColic pool, which has no built-in list (`?? []`), so the differential is empty.

mustNotMiss.note: Concomitant CBD stones must be considered (normal LFTs and CBD make it unlikely here — quality only).
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: iOS: fallback mode (DiagnosticDatabase.json does not decode): the gallstone ultrasound text is appended to the CC for routing and selects the biliaryColic pool, which has no built-in list (`?? []`), so the differential is empty.

emergencyLevel.note: Acute cholecystitis needs admission and surgical assessment the same day.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS ClinicalPathwayEngine: 'Right upper quadrant pain' selects the Biliary pathway but leaves acuity routine.

mustNotAlarm.note: No hypotension, tachypnoea or organ dysfunction: a sepsis alarm here is noise (alert fatigue).

recommended.note: TG18 severity grading drives the management flowchart.
recommended.knownGapNote: Web CDS has a TG18 cholangitis rule but none for cholecystitis.

values.note: Definite acute cholecystitis without any Grade II criterion (WBC >18, palpable tender RUQ mass, >72 h, marked local inflammation) or organ dysfunction = Grade I.
The record holds Murphy's sign, fever, WBC/CRP and characteristic ultrasound; auto-fill should reach Grade I rather than 'criteria not met'.
values.knownGapNote: iOS auto-fill sets only WBC >18 (Grade II criterion) and never the local-signs field, so it reads "criteria not met"; web clinical-scores needs manual Murphy/imaging ticks.

mustInclude.note: TG18 Grade I: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy when fit (CCI ≤5, ASA ≤2).

mustExclude.note: Gallbladder drainage is not first-line for Grade I in a fit patient.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: TG18 diagnostic criteria (A local, B systemic, C imaging) and severity grading (Grade III organ dysfunction; Grade II: WBC >18,000/mm³, palpable tender RUQ mass, duration >72 h, marked local inflammation; Grade I otherwise)
guideline.citation: Yokoe M, Hata J, Takada T, et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018: diagnostic criteria and severity grading of acute cholecystitis. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:41–54.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis
guideline.section: Grade I: early laparoscopic cholecystectomy if CCI ≤5 and ASA ≤2
guideline.citation: Okamoto K, Suzuki K, Takada T, et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018: flowchart for the management of acute cholecystitis. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:55–72.

guideline.name: Tokyo Guidelines 2018 — antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis
guideline.section: Antimicrobial selection by severity; blood cultures for Grade II/III
guideline.citation: Gomi H, Solomkin JS, Schlossberg D, et al. Tokyo Guidelines 2018: antimicrobial therapy for acute cholangitis and cholecystitis. J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci. 2018;25:3–16.

rationale: Base case for acute calculous cholecystitis. Checks recognition, TG18 Grade I grading (calculator and auto-fill), early laparoscopic cholecystectomy and that drainage is not offered first-line. Pertinent negatives ('no jaundice', 'no rigors') are written as clinicians write them.
